title: Multistep Problems with Rational Numbers
short: Mix fractions, decimals and percents and check with an estimate.

blocks.html: Real problems mix fractions, decimals and percents, and take several steps. You have every tool already: percents in stores, equations from stories and all four operations. The new part is planning and checking.

Read, estimate, then solve one step at a time. Switch between fractions, decimals and percents when it makes a step easier ($25\% = \frac{1}{4} = 0.25$). Compare your answer with the estimate at the end.

An estimate is a quick, rough answer you make before the exact one. Most slips in multistep problems, like a misplaced decimal point or a percent used as a whole number, make the answer far from the estimate, so the estimate catches them.

blocks.title: Discount, then tax
blocks.q: A \$45 jacket is 20% off, and then 6% sales tax is added. What is the total?
steps: Estimate: 20% off \$45 is about \$36, plus a little tax, so about \$38.
With tax: $1.06 \times 36 = 38.16$. Close to the estimate ✓.

blocks.title: A raise
blocks.q: Omar earns \$15 an hour and gets a 10% raise. How much does he earn for 30 hours at the new wage?

blocks.title: A leftover piece
blocks.q: A 10 ft board is cut into as many $1\frac{3}{4}$ ft pieces as possible. How much is left over?
steps: How many pieces fit: $$10 \div 1\frac{3}{4} = 10 \times \frac{4}{7} = \frac{40}{7} = 5\frac{5}{7}$$ so 5 whole pieces.
Left over: $10 - 8\frac{3}{4} = 1\frac{1}{4}$ ft. It is less than one piece ✓.
